pr_title: Fix(harness): raise the pydantic floor to 2.1 and drop look-around fr…
verdict: NOT READY TO MERGE - important: I1
strengths: SkillSpec.schema.json lines 591 and 597 carry the same pattern string as REL_PATH_PATTERN in strap_models.py:26, so the generated schema and the model agree and the drift test has nothing to flag.

The rewritten pattern accepts and rejects the same inputs as the old look-around form (leading slash or backslash, and a letter followed by a colon, are rejected; a lone letter is accepted), and it stays valid under both ECMA-262 and Rust regex syntax.
The SkillTarget description in the schema still matches the model docstring and the pattern's behavior.

test_relative_path_pattern_builds_on_the_default_regex_engine is a real guard: it builds a config-free TypeAdapter on REL_PATH_PATTERN, so reintroducing look-around fails it on current pydantic (rust-regex default) even though the CI interpreter never runs pydantic 2.1-2.4.

The relative-folder parametrization (`ab:c`, `9:`, `a`, `./skills`, `_x`) probes exactly the edges the look-around-free alternation must get right, mirroring the existing _ABSOLUTE rejection set and checking model and committed schema together.

The doctor floor tests stub only the _release seam and exercise the real check_modules / _installed / _requirement logic, including the equality boundary (2, 1) and the unknown-release (None) fallthrough; behavioral, not mock-chain wiring.
test_pydantic_below_its_release_floor_fails asserts the exact pip fix line, pinning that _requirement raises 'pydantic>=2' to 'pydantic>=2.1' in the remedy the developer copies.

REL_PATH_PATTERN without look-around (strap_models.py:26) accepts and rejects the same inputs as the old pattern: leading / or \, X: and X:foo are rejected; a bare letter, a digit-colon start and non-ASCII first characters pass. It also needs no special flags in Rust regex, Python re or the ECMA-262 regex the committed schema uses.

Dropping regex_engine from SkillTarget (strap_models.py:395) lets strap_models import on pydantic 2.1-2.4, which do not have that option; a grep finds no other look-around in any pydantic model pattern, so the 2.1 floor holds for the patterns.

_installed (doctor.py:145-154) passes a module whose release metadata is missing or unparseable instead of failing it, so an editable or vendored install with odd metadata still gets the major-version probe and is not reported as broken.
The FAIL detail and pip line from check_modules (doctor.py:167-172) name the raised floor (pydantic>=2.1), so a too-old install gets a pip command that actually upgrades it.

The new floor is stated the same way in CLAUDE.md:97, README.md:341 and the plugin.json `python` option description, so the dependency contract matches across the repo guide, the README and the plugin manifest.
The doctor SKILL.md modules row now describes the behavior doctor.py adds (a release floor on top of the major-version probe), which keeps the skill doc in line with the code.
The commit message lists every changed file with an accurate one-line change, and the new comments in strap_models.py and doctor.py explain why the floor and the look-around-free pattern exist.

doctor SKILL.md `modules` row matches the new code path: `_installed` fails a pydantic below `MIN_RELEASES` (2, 1) and the fix line carries `pydantic>=2.1`, as the row and the Afterward section describe.
The doctor skill's cross-references (README.md Python section, hpy header comment) stay accurate after the change; no orphan reference to a prior check name or path.

The floor bump lands in every top-level dependency statement together (CLAUDE.md, README.md option table, plugin.json option description, doctor SKILL.md), with tests/lib/test_doctor.py pinning the `pydantic>=2.1` detail and pip line.

The look-around-free REL_PATH_PATTERN matches exactly what the old pattern matched for non-empty strings (min_length=1 covers the empty case). It is exercised with accept sets (`ab:c`, `9:`, `a`) and reject sets (`c:x`, UNC, leading slash) against both the model and the committed schema.

test_relative_path_pattern_builds_on_the_default_regex_engine fails if look-around comes back on any pydantic version, because the current default engine refuses it too. It guards against regression and does more than restate the code.
doctor stays stdlib-only at import and degrades gracefully: an unknown release (`_release` returns None) falls back to the major-version probe, not a false failure.
The doctor tests replace only the metadata lookup and assert the visible status, detail and pip line. These are behavioral tests, not stub-call wiring.
The version bump and the dependency wording in CLAUDE.md, README, plugin.json and the doctor skill table move together, and the committed schema was regenerated alongside the model.

important.name: Runtime pydantic gates still accept 2.0, so the declared floor only exists in doctor
important.summary: This PR raises the floor to 2.1 because, per doctor.py:37-38, the plan models fail to import on pydantic 2.0. The probes users actually run still check only `hasattr(pydantic, 'model_validator')`: plan.py:95-106, plan_api.py:23-35 and pr_review.py:148-176. On a 2.0 interpreter those probes pass, the `from harness_lib import plan_models` import that follows fails, and the user gets a raw traceback where the `problem:` line should be. Missing pydantic is no better: the advice is still `pip install 'pydantic>=2'`, which pip treats as already met on 2.0. The comment at doctor.py:30 ('the same list pr_review.py gates on') is now false too: doctor applies a floor pr_review never checks. The fix landed where people go to diagnose problems and skipped the places that break.
fix: Move the floor check into a stdlib-only helper that all three probes call. harness_lib.doctor is already stdlib-only at import, so its `_installed`/`MIN_RELEASES` (or one `pydantic_floor_met()` function) can be imported before the pydantic-dependent modules. Change the three problem messages to `pydantic>=2.1` and the pip hints to `pip install 'pydantic>=2.1'`.

At minimum, set the requirement in pr_review.py:152 and the messages in plan.py:105 and plan_api.py:33 to `pydantic>=2.1`, add a `importlib.metadata.version('pydantic')` release check next to the `model_validator` probe, and fix the doctor.py:30 comment to match.

minor.name: pydantic floor lives in two places, and only doctor enforces it
minor.summary:
REQUIRED_MODULES still carries "pydantic>=2" (doctor.py:32, kept equal to pr_review._REQUIRED_MODULES by test_required_modules_match_the_pr_review_gate) while the real floor sits in a separate MIN_RELEASES (doctor.py:39). _requirement (doctor.py:135-138) rebuilds the pip line by string surgery: it discards whatever specifier the requirement carries and replaces it with the MIN_RELEASES floor, so raising the requirement past 2.1 later would make doctor print a lower floor than the one the gate asks for. The comment at doctor.py:30 still says this is 'the same list pr_review.py gates on', but the gates (pr_review.py, plan.py:105, plan_api.py:23-33) probe only model_validator, so pydantic 2.0 passes them and the plan models then die on a raw ImportError rather than the documented problem: line. CLAUDE.md, README and plugin.json now say pydantic>=2.1; the runtime gates and their messages still say >=2.

Also (runtime): The new _dist helper (doctor.py:141-142) repeats requirement.split(">=")[0], which _version still spells inline at doctor.py:158. _installed (doctor.py:153) also evaluates _release(_dist(requirement)) for every module, including referencing and jsonschema, which have no MIN_RELEASES entry, so each doctor run makes metadata lookups whose result is never used.

Also (roast): REQUIRED_MODULES (doctor.py:32) still lists the requirement as `pydantic>=2`. MIN_RELEASES (doctor.py:39) holds the real floor, and `_requirement` (doctor.py:135-138) rebuilds the `>=2.1` string from it just for the failure path. Anyone who bumps one copy has to know about the other. Also, `_dist` (doctor.py:141-142) duplicates the `requirement.split('>=')[0]` that `_version` still does inline at doctor.py:158.
fix: Raise the requirement string to "pydantic>=2.1" in both doctor.REQUIRED_MODULES and pr_review._REQUIRED_MODULES, derive the floor from the requirement text (parse the part after '>='), and drop MIN_RELEASES and the string rebuild in _requirement; update the plan.py and plan_api.py messages to name pydantic>=2.1.

Keep MIN_RELEASES but have _requirement emit the higher of the requirement's own floor and MIN_RELEASES, and reword the doctor.py:30 comment to say the pr_review gate checks the major version only while doctor also enforces MIN_RELEASES.
In _version replace `dist = requirement.split(">=")[0]` with `dist = _dist(requirement)`; in _installed return True early when `MIN_RELEASES.get(module)` is None before calling _release.

Write the floor once: set the tuple entry to `pydantic>=2.1` and parse the floor from the requirement string (the text after `>=`, split on `.`, as ints). Then drop MIN_RELEASES and `_requirement`, and have `_version` call `_dist`.
Keep MIN_RELEASES, but change the REQUIRED_MODULES requirement to `pydantic>=2.1` and replace `_version`'s inline split with `_dist(requirement)`.

minor.name: doctor modules row repeats the floor and overstates the check
minor.summary: plugins/harness/skills/doctor/SKILL.md:27 says the check fails when `pydantic>=2.1` ... is missing, or its pydantic is older than 2.1. The second clause repeats the first, since `pydantic>=2.1` being missing already covers an old release. The row also does not say that _installed in plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/doctor.py passes a pydantic whose release metadata cannot be read (found is None): an old pydantic with no readable version only gets the major-version probe.
fix: Reword the row to: `pydantic`, `referencing` or `jsonschema` is missing from that interpreter, or its pydantic is older than 2.1 (fail); the fix line pins `pydantic>=2.1`. An install whose version metadata cannot be read gets only the major-version probe.

minor.name: strap-skills SKILL.md still names the old pydantic>=2 floor
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/skills/strap-skills/SKILL.md:45 tells project-skill users to point HARNESS_PY at an interpreter with `pydantic>=2`. strap_models is the module whose import failed on old pydantic, which is the reason this PR exists, and CLAUDE.md:97, README.md:341, the plugin.json `python` option and doctor/SKILL.md:27 now all say `pydantic>=2.1`. So the one skill that depends on the fix still names the floor the PR retires. The user-facing problem lines in plugins/harness/scripts/plan.py:105, plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/plan_api.py:33 and the comment at plugins/harness/scripts/pr_review.py:148 also still read `pydantic>=2`.

Also (skill_package): The PR raises the floor to pydantic 2.1 in CLAUDE.md, README.md, plugin.json and the doctor skill's `modules` row (doctor now fails 2.0), and the motivating breakage was importing `strap_models`. The strap-skills skill, whose `red` and `freeze` gate runs those models, still tells the developer that `HARNESS_PY` needs an interpreter with `pydantic>=2`. An interpreter that satisfies strap-skills' stated requirement now fails `/harness:doctor`, so the two skills give the developer contradictory install guidance.

Also (roast): CLAUDE.md, README, plugin.json and the doctor skill all moved to `pydantic>=2.1`. The strap-skills skill, whose `strap_models` import is what this PR fixes, still tells project-skill users to point HARNESS_PY at an interpreter with `pydantic>=2`, so the lockstep update missed one file. The contract test tests/skills/test_strap_skills_project_profile_contract.py:24 checks for the substring `pydantic>=2`, which `pydantic>=2.1` still contains, so the edit is safe.
fix: In plugins/harness/skills/strap-skills/SKILL.md:45 change `pydantic>=2` to `pydantic>=2.1`. The contract test tests/skills/test_strap_skills_project_profile_contract.py:24 looks for the substring `pydantic>=2`, so it still passes.

Optionally change the `pydantic>=2` wording in the plan.py:105 and plan_api.py:33 messages (including their `pip install 'pydantic>=2'` hint) to `pydantic>=2.1`, so every place that names the floor agrees.

In plugins/harness/skills/strap-skills/SKILL.md line 45, change `pydantic>=2` to `pydantic>=2.1`, and update the `"pydantic>=2" in body` assertion in tests/skills/test_strap_skills_project_profile_contract.py:24 to `"pydantic>=2.1" in body` so the contract pins the new floor.

minor.name: No test pins MIN_RELEASES to the documented pydantic floor
minor.summary: The PR raises the documented floor to pydantic>=2.1 in four prose places (CLAUDE.md:97, README.md:341, plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:12, plugins/harness/skills/doctor/SKILL.md:27) and encodes it once in doctor.MIN_RELEASES. The new doctor tests hard-code the literal 'pydantic>=2.1' in their assertions (test_doctor.py:53-54) rather than deriving it, so a later floor bump in MIN_RELEASES would fail these tests while a drift between MIN_RELEASES and the README/plugin.json text would pass silently.
fix: Add a test that formats the floor from doctor.MIN_RELEASES['pydantic'] (e.g. 'pydantic>=' + '.'.join(map(str, floor))) and asserts that string appears in REPO_ROOT / 'README.md', plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and plugins/harness/skills/doctor/SKILL.md, spelling those file names in the source so tools/select_tests.py selects it.
At minimum, derive the expected requirement in test_pydantic_below_its_release_floor_fails from doctor.MIN_RELEASES instead of the literal.

minor.name: test_release expected value breaks on a pre-release pydantic
minor.summary: test_release_reads_the_installed_distribution builds its expected tuple with int(part) over pydantic.VERSION.split('.')[:3]. On a pre-release or dev build (e.g. '2.12.0b1', '2.13.0.dev0') int('0b1') raises ValueError, so the test errors in the expectation rather than in the code under test, while doctor._release itself handles that case through its leading-digits regex. The suffix-stripping branch of _release (doctor.py:129-132) is also never exercised: the test only reaches it with whatever release happens to be installed.
fix: Compare against importlib.metadata.version('pydantic') parsed the same tolerant way, or assert only the type/prefix: `found = doctor._release('pydantic'); assert found is not None and found[:2] == tuple(int(p) for p in re.match(r'\d+\.\d+', pydantic.VERSION).group(0).split('.'))`.

Add a parametrized test that monkeypatches doctor.importlib.metadata.version to return '2.4.2', '2.0.0b3', '2.10.0.dev1' and 'garbage', asserting (2, 4, 2), (2, 0, 0), (2, 10, 0) and None, so the regex path is pinned independently of the installed build.

minor.name: Module docstring omits the new relative-folder and regex-engine guards
minor.summary: The module docstring (lines 1-9) enumerates what the file pins and ends with 'target folders reject absolute paths in both the model and the schema'. The PR adds test_skill_target_accepts_relative_folder (accepted relative folders, model and schema) and test_relative_path_pattern_builds_on_the_default_regex_engine (no look-around in REL_PATH_PATTERN), neither of which the docstring names, so the stated contract of the file lags its tests.
fix: Extend the last sentence of the module docstring: '... that ``target`` folders reject absolute paths and accept repo-relative ones in both the model and the schema, and that ``REL_PATH_PATTERN`` compiles on pydantic's default regex engine (no look-around).'
